title: Call Conciliation Protocol and Stub API Sketch
content:
Context and motivation:

This is a personal sketch for a lightweight client-server protocol to 'conciliate' (merge/resolve) outputs from multiple inference routes and stubbed tools. The goal: provide a small, predictable contract that clients (SDKs, edge proxies) can use to 1) safely issue requests under fallbacks, 2) reconcile partial/duplicate/async tool responses, and 3) maintain idempotency and auditability while keeping server complexity bounded.

Why now:
- More apps use multiple execution tiers (hosted model variant, cheaper quantized variant, local client-side tool).
- We need a standardized pattern to avoid duplicate side-effects, inconsistent tool outputs, and confusing UX when multiple backends race or fall back.
- The console and tracing currently lack consistent objects to show how a final response was composed.

Non-goals:
- Not a full orchestration system. This is not intended to cover multi-model aggregation strategies (ensembles) beyond simple rules.
- Not addressing billing semantics here (that's separate).

High-level requirements:
- Idempotent by default: repeat attempts with same request id must not cause duplicate side-effects when tools are involved.
- Deterministic conciliation: given the same set of observations the server should produce a reproducible final event (for audit).
- Small footprint: minimal new primitives for the runtime and SDKs; rely on existing streaming/event hooks where possible.
- Observable: make it easy to reconstruct the decision tree for a given final response (for debugging).

Key concepts / terminology:
- call_id: client-assigned opaque id (UUID v4 recommended). Unique per logical user request (not per network retry).
- attempt_id: server- or client-assigned id for a single execution attempt (useful when there are retries/fallbacks).
- actor: origin of a partial result (e.g., model-a, model-b, local-tool-x, cache).
- fragment: a partial response chunk (text, structured object, tool result) with provenance metadata.
- conciliation policy: rule set describing how fragments are merged/selected (first-success, highest-confidence, union-merge, tool-override, etc.).
- stub: a synthetic response produced by a client-side or mock tool for offline testing; must declare is_stub=true.

API shapes (draft):

1) POST /v1/conciliate/call  (start a conciliated call)
Request JSON:
{
  "call_id": "<uuid>",
  "prompt": "...",
  "conciliation_policy": "first-success", // or custom policy id
  "timeout_ms": 12000,
  "allowed_actors": ["hosted-a","quantized-b","client-tool"],
  "metadata": {"user_tier": "pro", "trace_hint": "foo"}
}
Response (202 accepted, stream to follow):
{
  "call_id": "<uuid>",
  "attempt_id": "<attempt-uuid>",
  "status": "in_progress",
  "accepted_at": "2025-02-12T15:02:31Z"
}

Notes: metadata must only include strings (avoid nested objects in this draft). The SDK will stream fragments to the client.

2) Streaming fragments: Server sends SSE or websockets messages with this envelope (textual example):
{ "kind": "fragment", "call_id": "...", "attempt_id": "...", "fragment_id": "f-1", "actor": "hosted-a", "type": "text", "payload": "Hello", "confidence": "0.82", "is_stub": "false", "received_at": "..." }
{ "kind": "fragment", "...", "actor": "client-tool", "type": "tool", "payload": "{\"search_hits\":[...]}" }

3) Finalization message (server-initiated or client flush):
{ "kind": "finalized", "call_id":"...", "attempt_id":"...", "result_summary":"selected fragment f-3 by policy first-success", "final_payload_type":"text|structured", "final_payload":"...", "conciliation_trace":"trace-id-445" }

4) Conciliation trace object (stored server-side; trace id returned above). For the draft we don't expose structured trace via API, but we include a link id for console view.

Conciliation policies (examples):
- first-success: choose first fragment with type text|structured that passes quick sanity heuristics (no blacklisted tokens, not empty).
- tool-override: any tool fragment marked tool_override=true wins over model outputs.
- merge-union: for structured fragments (lists/maps) perform shallow union by actor precedence.
- highest-confidence: pick fragment with highest confidence field (requires confidence normalization).

Idempotency and side-effects tolerance:
- Tools must declare side_effects: none|idempotent|maybe_non_idempotent. Server should block auto-retries for maybe_non_idempotent unless client explicitly allows retry_by_policy=force.
- If a tool returns side_effects!=none the runtime records (call_id, attempt_id, fragment_id, tool_result_id) and surfaces a decision: replayable? compensatable? This is a sketch—actual compensating flows will be more involved.

Client stub semantics:
- Client-provided stubs must include is_stub=true and stub_origin="client"; server should never forward is_stub fragments to downstream billing/action hooks. Stubs are allowed for UX previews and local QA only.

State machine (ascii):

Client -> [POST /conciliate/call] -> SERVER(start attempt) -> attempt:waiting_for_fragments
    |-- receives fragments from actors (model/tool/cache) -> server stores fragments with timestamps
    |-- apply policy -> may finalize early -> send finalized msg -> DONE
    |-- timeout -> apply fallback policy (e.g., switch actor set) -> new attempt_id -> continue

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we allow client-provided conciliation policy functions (js-safe) to execute on the server? Risky for perf/sandboxing. For now allow only named, server-registered policies and an opt-in 'safe-js' set in future.
- Normalization of confidence scores: spec required so highest-confidence is meaningful. Need mapping doc from model-type->[0,1].
- Where does billing attribution land when final response is a merged union? For now attribute proportionally by token count per fragment (tracking needed).
- Console UX: expose conciliation_trace id and show fragment timeline, actor lanes, policy rule matches.

Backwards-compatibility / rollout path:
- v1: implement server-only policies; SDK adds call_id field and listens for SSE fragments. Fallback behaviour defaults to existing runtime flows.
- v1.1: add client-side stub declaration and trace link in SDKs; enable dev-mode UI to visually simulate fallback scenarios.

Quick SDK example (pseudo-js):
const callId = uuid();
const resp = await api.post('/v1/conciliate/call', {call_id: callId, prompt, conciliation_policy:'first-success'});
const evStream = connectSSE(`/v1/conciliate/events?call_id=${callId}`);
evStream.on('fragment', f => { renderPartial(f.payload); });
evStream.on('finalized', f => { renderFinal(f.final_payload); showTraceLink(f.conciliation_trace) });

Implementation notes for runtime team (ideas):
- Reuse existing fragment store used by streaming; add actor and confidence attributes to fragments index.
- Conciliation worker: small state machine that subscribes to fragment stream per attempt_id and runs policies (policy is a plugin with safe sandbox).
- Storage: retain conciliation_trace for 30 days by default; long-term retention as enterprise option.

Appendix: quick examples of edge cases
- Duplicate fragment from same actor with different payloads: prefer later fragment if policy=last-wins; otherwise, treat as conflict and escalate to merge policy.
- Partial tool then tool error: if tool marked idempotent and later tool-error fragment arrives, if a model fragment already chosen, leave choice intact unless override rule configured.

Sign-off / next steps (for me):
- Share with runtime + SDK folks, get feedback on: minimal envelope fields, side_effects model, stub handling, and storage cost estimates.
- Draft a short demo PR that implements 'first-success' policy and the SSE fragment envelopes (no UI).
- Create a small confluence id for conciliation_trace format and confidence normalization mapping.

Notes to self: keep names short in the envelopes; prefer strings instead of nested objects to simplify early rollout. Avoid exposing raw tool outputs to external billing pipelines unless explicitly flagged.
